The rename preserves binary resource encoding, but **breaks compatibility with supported old clients**. Keeping field number 7 is insufficient to call the release harmless.

Both [v1](/tmp/tal-skills-fieldmask-native-2026-10-15-r02/trials/source08-microservice-v3-fieldmask-symbolic-rename-02/workspace/project/profile-v1.proto:5) and [v2](/tmp/tal-skills-fieldmask-native-2026-10-15-r02/trials/source08-microservice-v3-fieldmask-symbolic-rename-02/workspace/project/profile-v2.proto:5) declare field 7 as a string. The binary payload therefore still supplies `"Lea"` to the renamed field, consistent with the retained decode observation. However, `update_mask.paths` contains symbolic descriptor names: retaining a numeric tag does not translate `"display_name"` into `"display_label"`. The [retained evidence](/tmp/tal-skills-fieldmask-native-2026-10-15-r02/trials/source08-microservice-v3-fieldmask-symbolic-rename-02/workspace/project/retained-request.json:7) explicitly records the old mask failing with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and no mutation. ProtoJSON naming rules are irrelevant to this binary-resource RPC.

- Accept the exact legacy path `display_name` and canonical path `display_label`, mapping both to the single v2 field before descriptor-path validation.
- Validate the entire normalized mask before mutation. Reject genuinely unknown paths; never silently discard them. If both aliases occur, treat them as one selection.
- Apply only selected fields. The decoded resource’s `bio: ""` must not overwrite stored `bio: "Keep"` when only the display field is selected.
- Keep one resource field at tag 7; the alias belongs in mask handling.
| `display_name` — supported old client | Success after alias normalization | `{"name":"profiles/U4","display_label":"Lea","bio":"Keep"}` |

An old client decoding the successful resource would see `display_name: "Lea"` at tag 7. The currently observed old-request rejection is the defect this proposal would fix.

The proposed rollout should make both paths available on every serving instance and any rollback target. Deployment order alone cannot repair immutable old-client masks. Retain the legacy alias throughout the required six-month support window. Provider owners should track actual legacy-path requests by client version, verify detection with a known legacy request, and coordinate migration with client owners. Retirement needs evidence covering infrequent or offline supported clients; a deadline or quiet telemetry alone is insufficient.
